meta.title: Maths tutor in Ealing | GCSE, A level and 11+ | Ruth Adeyemi
meta.description: Ruth Adeyemi, a former secondary school maths teacher, tutors GCSE, A level and 11+ maths in Ealing and online. Book a free first session.

rationale: A magazine feel suits a tutor whose selling point is ten years of teaching and a calm manner: cream paper, brown ink, one terracotta accent and a serif headline. Long readable text, a letter-like story and a single big quote carry the trust, while a drawing of the kitchen table and a hand-marked sentence give the page its own face.

props.statement: Maths lessons at a kitchen table in Ealing, with a teacher who spent ten years in a secondary school classroom.
props.detail: GCSE, A level and 11+ preparation. One to one in the week, groups of three on Saturdays, or online if that suits your family better.

props.before: Nearly every child who says they hate maths got stuck on
props.after: and nobody went back for it.

props.title: What I teach and how the lessons run

items.name: GCSE maths
items.description: We start from the topics that cost your child marks, not from chapter one. Past papers come later, once the gaps underneath have been filled.

items.name: A level maths
items.description: For students who understood school maths and now feel the pace has doubled. We slow down on the ideas, then practise until the method feels like theirs.

items.name: 11+ preparation
items.description: Maths for the entrance papers, taught so that a ten year old stays curious rather than frightened of the clock.

items.name: One to one, in the week
items.description: Just your child and me, at my kitchen table in Ealing or online. Good for catching up quickly or for pushing ahead.

items.name: Saturday groups of three
items.description: Three pupils at the same table. Children often ask each other the question they would not ask an adult.

props.title: Ten years at the front of a classroom, now at my own table
paragraphs: I taught maths in a secondary school for ten years. I liked the subject and I liked the pupils, but I never had enough time to sit beside the child who had quietly stopped following three weeks earlier.
So I started tutoring on my own. Now the pace is set by the child in front of me. If a fraction needs another ten minutes, it gets them.

Parents ask me about results, and that is fair. Grades matter, and we work towards them every week. But I have learned that the grade follows once a child stops being scared of the page, so that is where I begin.
Lessons happen at my kitchen table in Ealing, or online when that is easier for your family. In the week I teach one to one. On Saturdays I keep groups to three.
props.pullQuote: The grade follows once a child stops being scared of the page.

props.title: Before you book: what the free first session is like

pairs.answer: No. We work through a few problems together and I watch how they think. That tells me more than a score would.
As you prefer. Some parents sit in the corner for the first ten minutes, others go for a walk. Both are fine.

pairs.ask: What if my child hardly says a word?
pairs.answer: Quite common at the start. I do the talking and the questions are small, so there is no way to get it wrong.
I tell you honestly what I saw and whether one to one or the Saturday group would suit. If tutoring is not what your child needs, I will say so.

quote.text: My daughter used to hide her homework. Now she asks if she can do the hard questions first.
